identity.spiritualSignificanceShort: Kamakhya on Nilachal hill is among the best known Shakti shrines in India and is counted among the fifty-one shaktipeethas. It holds no image of the goddess: worship centres on a stone in a corner of the cave-like inner chamber carved with the yoni symbol and kept wet by a natural spring. Nine further shrines on the hill — Bhubaneswari, Kali, Tara, Chinnamasta, Bagala, Bhairavi, Dhoomavati, Matangi and Kamala — form with Kamakhya the Dasamahavidya, which makes the hill a centre for tantric worship as well as general pilgrimage.
sacredClassifications: Shakti Peetha — one of the 51 shaktipeethas

governance.establishedEra: The earlier temple was destroyed by Kala Pahar and the present structure was reconstructed in 1565 by Chilarai of the Koch dynasty
governance.founderPatron: Rebuilt in 1565 by Chilarai, then the reigning Koch ruler
governance.managingAuthority: Bardeuri Samaj, composed of the adult male members of four families, with the office of the Bor-Doloi and Saru-Doloi

narrative.documentedHistory:
The temple standing on Nilachal hill today dates from the sixteenth century: the earlier structure was destroyed by Kala Pahar, and it was reconstructed in 1565 by Chilarai, the reigning ruler of the Koch dynasty.

The building is laid out in three main chambers along an east-west axis. The western chamber is rectangular; the middle chamber is square and carries inscriptions and images of Naranarayana; the innermost chamber is cave-like and holds a yoni-shaped cleft in the bedrock fed by a natural spring. There is no idol or image of the goddess, worship being directed at the stone bearing the carved yoni symbol.

The hill carries a wider complex of shrines, including five dedicated to Shiva and three to Vishnu — Kedara, Gadadhara and Pandunath — alongside the nine Dasamahavidya temples.
narrative.architectureStyle: Three-chambered Assamese temple of the Nilachal type, rebuilt in the sixteenth century

visitingInfo.entryRules: Devotees must leave their footwear at the designated camps on the approach road. The entire Kamakhya complex and Nilachal hill is a declared no-tobacco zone.
visitingInfo.prasadInfo: The sanctum is closed from 13:00 to 14:30 each day for the cooked offerings to the goddess.
visitingInfo.officialContactNote: The sanctum closes entirely for the Ambubachi period each year and special-darshan tickets are suspended on the reopening days. Confirm the day's schedule and any darshan-pass arrangement with the Office of the Doloi, Maa Kamakhya Devalaya, before travelling.

openingHours.notes: Temple door opens for devotees at 08:00; the Snana of the Pithasthana is at 05:30 and Nitya puja at 06:00, before the doors open. Doors close at 13:00 for the cooked offerings.
Doors reopen for devotees at 14:30 and close for the night at 17:15; the Aarati of the goddess follows at 19:30.
The temple door is closed to devotees for the Ambubachi period — the official site gives 23 to 25 June for 2026 — and reopens on the morning of 26 June after the ritual bathing and the daily puja.

festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: Around 21–22 June; for 2026 the official site gives the closure as 23 to 25 June with reopening on 26 June
festivals.duration: Four days, of which the sanctum is shut for three
festivals.significance: Observed as the yearly menstrual cycle of the goddess. Assam Tourism describes it as a four-day festival marking the annual menstruation of Mother Earth; it is the temple's principal gathering and draws tantric practitioners from across India.
festivals.processionOrRituals: The temple door stays closed to devotees for the duration and reopens on the fourth morning after ritual bathing and the daily puja.
festivals.visitorAdvice: The sanctum cannot be entered during the closure. The Rs 501 special darshan is stated to be unavailable on 26 and 27 June because of the crowds, and devotees must leave footwear at the designated camps on the approach road.

festivals.gregorianRuleOrDate: A fortnight, from Krishna Navami to Sukla Navami of Aswina
festivals.significance: The principal autumn observance at the temple.
festivals.processionOrRituals: Includes the ritual bath of the deity with Panchagarva and bali offerings; Kumari Puja, the worship of a virgin girl as a manifestation of the goddess, forms part of the major pujas.

festivals.significance: Worship of Manasha, accompanied by the Deodhani dances.
festivals.processionOrRituals: Held in the Natmandir of the temple, with shamanistic Deodhani dancing.

festivals.significance: Observed as the marriage day of Devi Kamakhya.
